title: Jason White's 2003 Heisman: OU's Comeback Quarterback
question: How did Jason White win the Heisman after two knee injuries?
answer: Jason White, from Tuttle, Oklahoma, tore the ACL in each knee in 2001 and 2002, then threw for 3,744 yards and 40 touchdowns in 2003 to win the Heisman Trophy as Oklahoma's fourth winner.
summary: Tuttle native Jason White came back from two torn ACLs to win the 2003 Heisman with 40 TD passes, then won the Davey O'Brien Award again in 2004.
body: Jason White's Heisman is one of the great comeback stories in Sooner history. An all-state quarterback at Tuttle High, he stayed close to home and signed with Oklahoma, but tore the ACL in one knee in 2001 and the other in 2002. Many careers end there. His was just getting started.

In 2003 White played with remarkable efficiency, completing 265 of 414 regular-season passes for 3,744 yards, 40 touchdowns and only eight interceptions. The Sooners won their first 12 games and finished 12-2 after a loss to LSU in the BCS national championship game. White won the Heisman with 1,481 points, ahead of Pitt receiver Larry Fitzgerald and Ole Miss quarterback Eli Manning, and became the fourth Sooner to win the trophy. He also collected the Davey O'Brien Award, AP Player of the Year honors and the Jim Thorpe Courage Award.

Because of his injuries, White received a sixth season of eligibility, and the Heisman Trust notes he is the only winner to be granted one. He made it count: 3,205 yards and 45 touchdowns in 2004, a third-place Heisman finish, a second straight Davey O'Brien Award, plus the Maxwell Award and the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award. He left Norman as OU's career leader in passing yards and touchdown passes.

His knees kept him from an NFL career. He signed with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2005 but retired that summer. White stayed in Oklahoma as a businessman, and a bronze statue of him joined OU's Heisman Park in 2007.
